name: חִזְקִיָּהוּ
gloss: Yahweh is my strength; or Yahweh strengthens
summary: Above all Hezekiah son of Ahaz, king of Judah, who trusted in Yahweh (2Ki 18:5), opened and repaired the doors of the house of Yahweh in his first year (2Ch 29:3), and when Sennacherib came “took courage (וַיִּתְחַזַּק) and built up all the broken wall … and strengthened the Millo” and told the people, “be strong and courageous … with us is Yahweh our God to help us” (2Ch 32:5, 7–8); he was sick and recovered (Isa 39:1, וַיֶּחֱזָק), and his men copied out proverbs of Solomon (Pro 25:1). He is in the genealogy of Jesus (Mat 1:9–10, Ἑζεκίας). The name is also borne by an ancestor of Zephaniah (Zep 1:1), the head of a family of returned exiles listed with Ater (Ezr 2:16; Neh 7:21; 10:18), a son of Neariah of David's line (1Ch 3:23), and in the longer spelling יְחִזְקִיָּהוּ by Jehizkiah son of Shallum, an Ephraimite chief who sent back the captives of Judah (2Ch 28:12–15). The name is חִזְקִי “my strength” (the form of Psa 18:2, “I love you, Yahweh, חִזְקִי”) with יָהוּ, or, in the spelling יְחִזְקִיָּהוּ, the verb “Yahweh strengthens”; scripture does not explain it, but his story is told in the root's own words.

evidence.note: “חִזְקִיָּה son of Ahaz king of Judah began to reign.”
“He trusted in Yahweh the God of Israel.”
“I love you, Yahweh, חִזְקִי”: the noun חֵזֶק with “my”, the first part of the name.
He opened the doors of the house of Yahweh “וַיְחַזְּקֵם”.
“וַיִּתְחַזַּק, and built up all the broken wall … וַיְחַזֵּק אֶת־הַמִּלּוֹא.”
“חִזְקוּ וְאִמְצוּ … with him is an arm of flesh, but with us is Yahweh our God to help us”; and the people leaned on the words of יְחִזְקִיָּהוּ.
The king of Babylon heard “that he had been sick וַיֶּחֱזָק”.
“I have heard your prayer, I have seen your tears; behold, I will heal you.”
Proverbs of Solomon “which the men of חִזְקִיָּה king of Judah copied”.
“Did Hezekiah king of Judah … not fear Yahweh and entreat his favour?”
Ἑζεκίας in the genealogy of Jesus Christ; the Peshitta writes חֵזַקיָא.
Zephaniah “son of Amariah, son of חִזְקִיָּה”.
“The sons of Ater, of Hezekiah (לִיחִזְקִיָּה), ninety-eight.”
“Ater, חִזְקִיָּה, Azzur”, among those who sealed the covenant.
“The sons of Neariah: Elioenai, וְחִזְקִיָּה, and Azrikam, three.”
Among the heads of the sons of Ephraim, “וִיחִזְקִיָּהוּ son of Shallum”.

note: Takes h.bs.ai (the name, 131 tokens, all spellings: חִזְקִיָּהוּ, חִזְקִיָּה, יְחִזְקִיָּהוּ, יְחִזְקִיָּה) and h.bs.ak (יְחִזְקִיָּהוּ, a zero-token cross-reference). TIPNR records Jehizkiah son of Shallum (2Ch 28:12) and Hizkiah son of Neariah (1Ch 3:23) under their own keys; they bear the same name and are tagged here. TIPNR's Hezekiah@Neh.10.17 is Neh 10:18 in the Hebrew numbering. The reading “Yahweh is my strength” takes חִזְקִי as the noun חֵזֶק with the suffix, as in Psa 18:2; the יְ‑ spelling reads as an imperfect, “Yahweh strengthens”. Both are readings of the form; no verse gives the meaning. Wiktionary links an Akkadian Ḫazaqiyau (Assyrian records of the king), not followed to an edition.
